summary: This joint resolution terminates the August 11, 2025 presidential emergency declaration on crime in the District of Columbia, ending federal authority under the Home Rule Act to direct the Metropolitan Police Department.

scores.thoughts: The bill terminates a presidential emergency declaration regarding crime in DC. The preamble references federal blocking of $1B in DC local revenues for public safety, but the resolution itself does not alter federal spending levels, authorize expenditures, or change appropriations. No direct or meaningful impact on government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, tax policy, revenue collection, or any form of taxation.
No references to healthcare systems, coverage, funding, or policy in the bill text.
The bill addresses a crime emergency declaration but makes no mention of firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No content related to immigration, border policy, or immigrant protections.
The legislation has zero connection to reproductive rights or abortion policy.
No provisions affecting military or defense spending or policy.
No environmental, climate, or regulatory provisions present.
Mentions of public safety funding in the preamble are incidental; the bill does not expand or reduce welfare programs, food assistance, or similar safety-net policies.
The preamble references schools in passing when discussing blocked DC revenues, but the operative text does not address education funding, policy, or school choice.
No engagement with drug decriminalization, enforcement, or related policies.

The bill directly terminates a presidential 'crime emergency' declaration that would have allowed federal direction of DC police. The preamble emphasizes declining crime rates and criticizes the emergency action, indicating opposition to expanded federal enforcement measures in this context. This gives the bill a modest tangential relationship to criminal justice policy favoring local control over stricter federal intervention.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions.
No fiscal policy, deficit, or debt-reduction measures.
No provisions concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No foreign aid or international assistance content.
No election administration, voting access, or election integrity measures.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance provisions.
No labor, union, or worker-protection provisions.
No religious liberty, civil rights, or anti-discrimination provisions.
